title: Bolden's playing style and the Panama rags
summary: Bolden played mostly straight music loudly, could read, and was heard across the river.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Could you describe Bolden's style? Did he sound like anybody that you might have heard? Does he remind you of any of the other type of players?
Well, I'll tell you, how Buddy played, Buddy played straight music mostly, but loud. The only random music I hear Buddy played was like blues, pallet on the flow, and them kind of things.
No rag? Huh?
Rag, yeah. First time I ever heard of Panama. Now you know they had two Panama rags. I didn't know. Well, they had two Panama rags. And Buddy used to read.
Buddy could read?
Sure, Buddy could read. Buddy they read. Frank Lewis could read Clarendon's music.
What were the two Panamas?
Well, after, they had another Panama pluppets, the one they're playing now. You see, I could hum the other one, the first one to you.
Why don't you?

That one goes. See, that's the first one. Now the other one. That's a typical rap. The other one. Diddle-de-ding-de-ding-ding. Diddle-ding-de-ding-ding-ding-ding-ding-ding. That's the one I'm using now.

The other one, I think, was it composed by Seymour, S-E. Is it a red copy? I have an old sheet. Music of Panama, too. A different composer. It might be Seymour, S-E-Y-M-O-U-R, something like that. It might be the one. And the other is but Tyler, usually. Tyers. Tyers. Yeah, yeah, Tyers. I think there's a West End. The other, I think, is Seymour, something like that. A red copy. Do you remember? Was that a red sheet?
Mm-hmm. I'm correct.
I have that old sheet.
I have the first Panama.
Was Bolden playing that tune? Is that?
Yeah. Bolden used to play that.
That's when he first heard it. You mean the second Panama?
Oh, the first Panama.
The first Panama.
I never did yet. He played the second Panama. Oh, no.
And he played straight off the music, or would he play variations?
Well, he'd play off his music, but he's so loud. He'd play with a really vim.
They have a good tone?

Oh, yeah. A good tone. A blasting tone. Frank Hardy says, now we're going to play at the Globes all the night. Frank would tell all the people now, Jay's, to go by the Canal Street Ferry on the other side of the river and you'd hear him play. You know, way up in my house mostly. Mm-hmm.
Playing across the river in other words.
Yeah. And you'd hear him playing. Really? Out on the floor. He'd be playing back at the auditorium at the Globes Hall. He'd be playing at the Globes Hall.
And you could hear him across the river? I mean, you'd hear him. He'd be playing.
He'd be playing. And no joke.
